```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(AKCatchments)
options(AKCatchments.cache = file.path(tempdir(), "ak_vignette_cache"))
```

Alder cover for Wrangell-St. Elias catchments from the NPS WRST Land Cover
Mapping Project (Geographic Resource Solutions and ABR, 2004-2007; 28.5 m;
NPS DataStore 2171667), for the southern catchments outside the ACCS alder
map (`vignette("alder-accs")`). Its 10,062 spectral signatures carry cover
attributes from field and aerial-photo plots; `ak_alder(source = "nps_wrst")` averages
their alder cover over each catchment. Columns are prefixed `alnus_wrst_`,
so they sit beside the ACCS columns for calibration.

Input, as for every layer: catchments (sf polygons with `site_code`, one
row per catchment, any CRS; a single `ak_delineate()` result, a list of
them, `ak_catchments()` output or your own polygons). Chunks that download
data are not run when this vignette is built; chunks that only compute
are. The other layers are listed in `vignette("delineation")`, section 7.

## 1. Getting the data

Automatic, once: the detailed vegetation package is downloaded from the NPS
DataStore into the cache's `nps_wrst_veg/` folder and unpacked (nested
zips included); the cells per signature are counted once and saved
(`signature_cells.csv`). Redistribution terms are not stated by NPS:
confirm before sharing derived tables.

```{r prefetch, eval = FALSE}
ak_prefetch(x, layers = "alder/nps_wrst")
```

## 2. Using it

```{r use, eval = FALSE}
d <- ak_delineate(lat = 63.7255, lon = -148.9670, site_code = "SITE-001")   # one catchment
ak_alder(d, source = "nps_wrst")                            # one catchment

x <- ak_catchments(pts)                                  # many: data frame of site_code, lat, lon
x <- ak_alder(x, source = "nps_wrst")                       # columns appended to x, provenance recorded
ak_provenance(x)

ak_alder(sf::read_sf("hand_catchments.gpkg"), source = "nps_wrst")   # your own polygons
```

`unrecorded = "class_mean"` (default) or `"zero"` sets alder for
signatures whose plots recorded life forms only (section 4).

## 3. What you get

`site_code`, `alnus_wrst_cover`, `alnus_wrst_coverage_pct`,
`alnus_wrst_cover_se`, `alnus_wrst_cover_lo95`, `alnus_wrst_cover_hi95`,
`alnus_wrst_unrecorded_pct` (share of the mapped area whose alder comes
from class means, or is 0), `alnus_wrst_cover_flag` (`outside_map`,
`partial_coverage`, `error_exceeds_cover`).

## 4. Uncertainty: how it is computed

The ACCS map stops at about
61-61.8 N, so much of southern Wrangell-St. Elias has no value. The NPS
WRST land cover map (2004-2007, 28.5 m) covers the whole park. Its 10,062
spectral signatures carry cover attributes from field and aerial-photo
plots; `ak_alder(source = "nps_wrst")` averages their alder cover over the catchment.
Aerial-photo plots recorded life forms only, so about half the mapped area
has no alder by species: `unrecorded = "class_mean"` gives it the class's
mean from plots that did record it (`alnus_wrst_unrecorded_pct` says how
much), `"zero"` sets it to 0. Each signature's error is the SD of alder
among recorded signatures of its class; errors are independent between
signatures and shared by every pixel of one, so the catchment SE is exact.
Misclassification, source-wide bias and change since 2004-2007 are not in
it: calibrate against ACCS where both maps exist and carry the calibration
error into the sites that only have the NPS value.

## 5. Checking and validating it

The map is a different product, years and method from ACCS, so it is used
by **calibrating it against ACCS** where both exist, then predicting
ACCS-scale alder at the southern sites. Look at the overlap first (live
tests P08 and H09 report it):

```{r calibrate, eval = FALSE}
both <- x |> ak_alder() |> ak_alder(source = "nps_wrst") |>    # the two products' columns differ
  sf::st_drop_geometry() |>
  dplyr::filter(alnus_coverage_pct >= 90, alnus_wrst_coverage_pct >= 90)
cor(both$alnus_cover, both$alnus_wrst_cover)          # weak correlation: not worth calibrating
plot(alnus_cover ~ alnus_wrst_cover, both)
south <- ak_alder(x, source = "nps_wrst") |> dplyr::filter(!site_code %in% both$site_code)
range(south$alnus_wrst_cover)                         # beyond the overlap range = extrapolation
```

Fit the calibration with error in both variables (both columns have SEs),
in your analysis rather than in the package: it is a modelling choice.
Compare `unrecorded = "class_mean"` with `"zero"`: if conclusions change,
the unrecorded share is driving them.

## 6. Pitfalls

- About half the mapped area usually has no species-level alder record:
  check `alnus_wrst_unrecorded_pct`.
- 2004-2007 imagery; alder has expanded since, so expect an offset against
  ACCS.
- Coastal Sitka alder and interior alder are one signal here.
- Misclassification is not in the SE (no accuracy assessment was found).

## References

- Geographic Resource Solutions and ABR Inc. (2008). Wrangell-St. Elias National Park and Preserve land cover mapping project. NPS DataStore 2171667.
